### BR-ID-09 — Service accounts and delegation

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Connectors and automated tasks shall use individually managed service identities with limited scope, expiry and an accountable owner. A worker's session shall not become a reusable unrestricted credential for an agent.

Acceptance: Revoking a connector credential stops its new calls without disabling unrelated connectors; audit identifies both initiating user and executing service.

### BR-ID-08 — Correctable identity links

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

External programme identifiers shall retain issuer, verification state and link history. Wrong matches, merges and transfers require a controlled correction process that preserves original references and downstream impact.

Acceptance: An authorised correction unlinks the wrong identity, flags affected submissions and records which external changes remain unresolved.

### BR-ID-07 — Household and proxy boundaries

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Household relationships, caregivers and authorised representatives shall be recorded separately from account access. A family contact number shall not grant access to a member's private history or authorise disclosure.

Acceptance: A caregiver and household head can receive only the information permitted by the relevant relationship and authorisation rules.

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

A person shall be able to receive a local record and permitted workflow without an ABHA number, personal phone or biometric identifier. External identity linking shall be a separate authorised process.

Acceptance: A person lacking all three completes an eligible pilot encounter without a fabricated external identifier.

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

The platform shall search permitted records using identifiers and selected demographics, present possible matches and support uncertain identities. A name or phone number alone shall not trigger an automatic merge.

Acceptance: Same-name, shared-phone, spelling-variant and twin cases remain distinct unless an authorised reviewer resolves the identity link.

### BR-ID-04 — Caseload assignment and transfer

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Households, patients and tasks shall have effective assignment dates and responsible teams. Transfer shall preserve open work, restrict former access and identify unresolved responsibility gaps.

Acceptance: Transferring a worker's caseload moves eligible open tasks, records acknowledgement and prevents duplicate ownership or orphaned urgent tasks.

### BR-ID-03 — Authentication and recovery

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Workers shall use an approved authentication method appropriate to devices and connectivity. Privileged roles require a second factor. Recovery and device replacement shall verify identity and revoke superseded credentials.

Acceptance: Recovery cannot be completed using patient data or a shared phone number alone; privileged access remains blocked without the required factor.

### BR-ID-02 — Scoped permissions

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Access shall be constrained by tenant, role, assignment, programme, facility or geography, purpose and action. The server shall enforce the effective permission set for reads, writes, searches, exports and tool calls.

Acceptance: Negative tests cover each boundary and prove that hidden screens or manipulated requests cannot expand access.

criteria.literal_source_section:
### BR-ID-01 — Workforce lifecycle

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

The platform shall support invitation or approved import, identity verification, role assignment, activation, suspension, reassignment and removal. Every account shall belong to an accountable organisation; shared credentials shall not be the operating model.

Acceptance: A suspended user's online access and pending privileged actions are revoked within the NFR limit, with offline limits disclosed.
criteria.authority: Retained source; independent source approval and release applicability unverified.

criteria.literal_acceptance: Session, background job and reconnect tests enforce the limit and record the residual offline window.
criteria.literal_source_section:
### NFR-09 — Online revocation

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Role removal or account suspension shall stop new online access and actions within 5 minutes. A disconnected device is constrained by its offline grant and local lock policy; it cannot be promised immediate remote revocation.

Verification: Session, background job and reconnect tests enforce the limit and record the residual offline window.

criteria.literal_source_section:
### BR-UX-08 — Low literacy and field use

Priority: Should; original release: R1.

Common actions shall use short labels, clear touch targets and a small number of steps. Audio guidance shall be available only on demand to avoid disclosure in a shared setting. Progress shall not rely on colour alone.

Acceptance: Representative workers complete the principal tasks under the defined field usability protocol, including noisy and private-entry conditions.

criteria.literal_source_section:
### BR-UX-07 — Resume interrupted work

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

An interrupted visit shall reopen at its last durable state with captured data, outstanding questions and pending actions. Users shall not repeat a successfully recorded measurement solely because a screen or connection was lost.

Acceptance: App restart, incoming call and network-loss scenarios retain every field previously shown as durably saved.

criteria.literal_source_section:
### BR-UX-06 — Status that reflects reality

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

The application shall distinguish saved on device, saved on server, awaiting review, submitted, accepted, rejected and unresolved. A general completion tick shall never imply that every destination accepted a record.

Acceptance: Simultaneous success in one programme and failure in another produces separate visible statuses and a specific recovery action.

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Local completion, external acceptance and service completion shall be distinct. Cancelling a local task shall not falsely cancel an accepted external transaction; a separate authorised correction or cancellation request is required.

Acceptance: Cancellation after submission reports the actual destination state and generates any remaining reversal task.

### BR-UX-05 — Language and accessibility

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

The pilot shall support approved interface, speech and content languages, initially Hindi and English if suitable for the selected site. Critical content shall have reviewed translations. Numeric values, units and names shall survive language changes.

Acceptance: The same encounter retains meaning across supported languages and passes the defined accessibility and language-specific task tests.

### NFR-15 — Language quality

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Critical UI, counselling and escalation content shall receive qualified human review in each supported language. Numeric extraction, negation and clinical terms require task-specific evaluation; aggregate speech word error rate alone is insufficient.

Verification: Reviewers accept the language corpus, and all safety-critical benchmark cases meet the approved pass criteria.

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

The workspace shall display confirmed facts, uncertain facts, missing information and proposed actions as separate readable elements. A conversational answer shall not be the only way to discover task status.

Workers shall be able to speak, type or use structured questions for the same core workflow. Voice shall be optional; background listening shall be disabled. Users shall control recording, playback and deletion before submission.
